authoring_note: Written before any production run of this round. Two probe runs (single hull, V=1.0 m/s, one seed each) were used only to size the discretisation and to confirm that a single realisation has a tens-of-percent seed spread; they are not part of the reported data set and do not enter any figure or verdict.
question: Does a three-ship column formation in a broken-ice channel save ice resistance, how does that saving depend on spacing (1L-5L) and speed (0.5-2.0 m/s), and is the single-ship limit consistent with the Lindqvist (1989) three-component analytic anchor?

hypotheses.H1_calibration: The DEM single-ship ice load agrees with the Lindqvist (1989) three-component anchor converted to the case caliber within 15% at every swept speed.
hypotheses.H2_saving: The column saving decreases monotonically as the spacing grows (the lead's cleared corridor is re-filled by cross-channel drift), for every swept speed.
hypotheses.H3_convergence: The reported ice load is particle-count convergent: the grid-convergence index of the N, 2N, 4N family is below 5% and the family converges monotonically.

caliber_declaration.ship: L = 80 m, B = 20 m, rectangular box hull (planar 2-D kinematics; no bow, no entry angle, no heave of the hull).
caliber_declaration.ice: h = 0.7 m, 8/10 concentration, hexagonal jittered field, mean floe radius 10 m (floe diameter = ship beam).
caliber_declaration.environment: No wind. A cross-channel drift of 0.05 m/s represents the current-driven re-closure of the corridor the lead has cleared; its sensitivity band is 0.03 / 0.05 / 0.08 m/s.
caliber_declaration.numerics: Constant contact CFL: base dt = 0.008 s at the base floe radius, dt scaled with the floe radius in the refinement family; sample every 5 steps.
caliber_declaration.measurement_window: A hull contributes samples only while its centre is inside the ice field at least L/2 from either longitudinal edge and t >= 60 s. The reported per-hull load is the time mean of the upstream contact reaction over that window; the formation total is the sum over hulls.
caliber_declaration.ensemble: Three floe-field realisations (seed offsets 0, 1, 2) for every physical case; the reported value is the ensemble mean and the error bar is the standard error of the mean.
caliber_declaration.lindqvist_conversion: Level-ice Lindqvist three-component total in the case caliber, primary point alpha = 20 deg, mu = 0.05; the full band alpha in {15, 20, 30} deg x mu in {0.05, 0.10, 0.15} is reported. Coefficient provenance stays WITHHELD (primary paper not readable offline) and is carried through from src/tensordem/level_ice/formula.py.

metrics: M1 single-ship ice load (ensemble mean, N) versus Lindqvist total (N): relative deviation, per swept speed.
M2 saving = 1 - R_formation_total / (3 R_single) per (speed, spacing), ensemble mean +/- SEM, plus the paired estimator 1 - R_total/(3 R_lead) that removes the single-ship reference noise.
M3 monotonicity of M2 against spacing at fixed speed (non-increasing), strict and with a one-SEM tolerance.
M4 grid-convergence index of the N/2N/4N particle family for the single-ship and the 3-ship column load, with the observed order and the monotone/oscillatory verdict.
M5 numerical controls: timestep halving at the base mesh; cross-channel drift sensitivity band.

decision_rules.C1: PASS iff |relative deviation| < 15% at every swept speed for the pre-declared primary caliber; otherwise FAIL or WITHHELD.
decision_rules.C2a: PASS iff the saving is non-increasing in spacing at every swept speed, using the paired estimator with a one-SEM slack (the strict verdict is reported alongside).
decision_rules.C2b: PASS iff both refinement families converge monotonically (observed order defined, asymptotic ratio >= 1).
decision_rules.C3: PASS iff the GCI of both refinement families is below 5%.

out_of_domain_rule: The Lindqvist bending + submersion terms are a floor for any model that carries a continuous ice cover: a DEM load below that floor cannot be brought inside 15% by refinement, so a C1 failure whose cause is a load below the floor is registered as a capability gap (model-form), not as a numerical defect. The test is computed and stored (dem_below_anchor_floor).
alternatives_considered: A1 compare against the full Lindqvist total in the level-ice caliber (primary).
A2 compare against the Lindqvist bending + submersion floor (mechanism-resolved; the channel model has no crushing wedge).
A3 report only the formation saving (a ratio) and declare the absolute caliber WITHHELD. Rejected unless C1 fails, because the absolute number is what a designer would use.

controlled: floe field generator and seed base

confounders: Rigid discs cannot bend or break, so the model has no flexural-failure mechanism; the level-ice Lindqvist anchor contains one.
The 2-D hull has no entry angle, so the anchor's crushing term is out of domain (alpha = 90 deg diverges) and any finite alpha is a substitute.
The thickness of every floe is 0.7 m +/- 0, so the anchor's thickness dependence cannot be exercised here.
The cross-channel drift is a modelling choice; it is the only mechanism that can re-fill the lead's corridor and therefore the only source of a spacing dependence.

Contacts are penalty springs; the measured instantaneous load contains rare spikes of O(1 MN) against a mean of O(10 kN), so the time mean is a heavy-tailed statistic and the seed spread is reported instead of hidden.
repetitions: 3 seeds per physical case (134 DEM runs in total), 5 dm-spacing points x 7 speeds x 3 seeds for the saving surface.
stopping_rule: Stop after the pre-registered 134 cases have run once. No case is re-run with a different seed to improve the result, and no threshold is revised after inspecting results. A case that blows up is reported as such, not replaced.
analysis_predeclared: The collector benchmarks/w25_formation_collect.py computes every number in the artifact from the raw per-run JSON ledgers; no value is hand-typed. Verdicts are computed programmatically and an honest FAIL is never overwritten.
safety_and_resource_limits: DEM runs on the TensorDEM cluster queue (loong64 nodes); one process per case, single-threaded; total budget 14400 s wall clock via sharded submission.
interpretation_limits: A C1 PASS would support the absolute caliber; a C1 FAIL with dem_below_anchor_floor = true means the reported absolute load is a broken-ice channel loading, not a level-ice resistance, and only ratio statements (saving) should be read as validated by this experiment.
